children: Japan’s leading economic index, which gauges the outlook for economic activity in the coming months using indicators such as job offers and consumer sentiment, increased to 117.9 in July 2026 from a downwardly revised 116.2 in June, preliminary estimates showed.

It was the highest level since January 2014, supported by the government’s record fiscal budget, which included comprehensive measures to ease cost-of-living pressures and emergency energy support to cushion the impact of the Middle East conflict, while inflation remained close to the BOJ’s 2% target.
Meanwhile, the unemployment rate declined to 2.4% in July, its lowest level since July 2025, pointing to resilient labor market conditions, although employment was at a four-month low.
Consumer confidence also improved to a six-month high, amid households’ stronger views on overall livelihood.

title: Japan Leading Economic Index Highest Since 2014
